Comparative round-trip experiments (group32, mixed int8/int4) on temp files, measuring loaded validation for each encoding before committing — near-harness verification behavior.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly reloaded the checkpoint through its own loader/dequant path, confirmed the byte cap, computed loaded local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy, and explicitly asserted the cross-entropy/logits forward contract — and crucially caught the int4 dequant round-trip degradation (in-memory vs loaded gap), which is the signature level-8 behavior of grader-faithful self-verification. It falls short of level 10 because verification was run as manual milestone checks rather than a single reusable automated gate on every iteration, and it did not secure explicit margin against the threshold. This places it firmly at the level-8 anchor.
